body:
I had a lot of confusion working with Uniform Sets, which turns out have a similar behavior: if any of the RIDs they reference gets freed, then the uniform set is automatically freed (or so I was told, it's a bit unsure).

This is causing trouble in my project because now I try to free them after use ([as the doc suggests](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingdevice.html#class-renderingdevice-method-uniform-set-create)).
However sometimes it works, and sometimes it prints `Attempted to free invalid ID` this because it has already been "auto-freed".

Trouble is, sometimes I really have to free them [otherwise they leak because Godot can't guess that I'm re-using buffers](https://github.com/Zylann/godot_voxel/pull/735#issuecomment-2707694765), and so other times I have to NOT free them myself because of Godot doing it by itself. Figuring this out manually is annoying, when the behavior seems to exist for convenience in the first place.

Right now I ended up freeing uniform sets always before freeing anything else, to keep things simple. Though it kinda defeats the point of the auto-freeing behavior.

At the very least, this needs to be documented, including in areas that tell you to free such RIDs.

I'm having the same problem working with compute shaders.
When i free all my rids, only the pipeline and the uniform set rids complains: "attempted to free invalid ID", even if i check before if they are valid using rid.IsValid.

i'm using C# and Godot 4.5.1

> I'm having the same problem working with compute shaders. When i free all my rids, only the pipeline and the uniform set rids complains: "attempted to free invalid ID", even if i check before if they are valid using rid.IsValid.

You should be using [render_pipeline_is_valid](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingdevice.html#class-renderingdevice-method-render-pipeline-is-valid) and [uniform_set_is_valid](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingdevice.html#class-renderingdevice-method-uniform-set-is-valid) respectively. `RID.is_valid()` only tells if if the handle is non-zero, to check if the resource being pointed to by the RID handle is valid, you need to use the check for that type of resource. 

Ultimately, the docs need to be updated to clarify which types of resources depend on other resources and will get freed when those other resources are freed.
